title: Fuse BF16 K=V=64 GLA intra-tile output on gfx936
mechanism: The fused producer computes a full 64x64 intra-chunk A tile and immediately consumes it in A@V within the same CTA. For K=V=64 there is one K tile and one V tile, so this avoids writing the FP32 A intermediate to global memory, reading it again in the output kernel, and launching that separate output stage without duplicating A computation.
applicability: Validated on Hygon BW/gfx936, BF16 inference with K=64 and V=64, no gradients, no initial state, no final-state output, non-varlen input, and state_v_first=False. Seven shapes varying B, T, and H passed output checks and three alternating-order A/B rounds.
transferable_lesson: For small square GLA head dimensions where a CTA can hold one complete intra-chunk A tile and one V tile, test fusing A@V with output to remove the global intermediate and launch. Match BC/K/V tile widths so the fused path does not decompose a baseline-wide tile into repeated subtiles. Always compare end-to-end latency and resource pressure; larger V can make fusion slower.
limitations: Do not enable for K/V=128: the broad fusion candidate was 1.5–1.7x slower on tested cases. FP16, FP32, varlen, initial/final state, state_v_first, backward, and dimensions other than K=V=64 are not validated. rocprofv2 kernel-trace did not finish, so no PMC/LDS-bottleneck claim is made. The full public benchmark improvement was limited to the eligible D=64 case, while the seven-case held-out family produced the recorded geomean gain.
